newsitem.title: USA: Toshiba unveils first desktop PC in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba unveils first desktop PC in U.S.

text.p: Toshiba Corp said Tuesday it was entering the U.S. desktop computer market by launching its Infinia line of home PCs.
The company estimated selling prices at $1,699 to $2,799 for the Infinia line.
Toshiba said it plans to expand its offerings to include business desktops during the first quarter of 1997 and servers by early 1998.
"Our move into the desktop market, combined with our continued growth in portable computers, well positions us to strengthen our market leadership," the company said.

"Currently, with our portable offering, we're the country's eighth largest computer company. By adding desktop computers to our mix, we have our sights set on the number five spot, and we'll be there by the end of 1997," it said in a statement released in New York.
Toshiba said the Infinia line uses Intel Corp's Pentium 133MHz, Pentium 166MHz and Pentium 200MHz chips and has hard drives ranging up to three gigabytes.

The line also has 16 megabyte (MB) or 32MB standard EDO memory, expandable to 128MB, as well as a 28.8 kilobits per second (kbps) modem, with software upgradable to 33.6 kbps and Digital Simultaneous Voice Data capabilities.

The Infinia line also includes Toshiba's InTouch Modules and InTouch Remote, which provide one-touch access for checking telephone messages, making a phone call, playing a compact disc or tuning into TV or FM radio.
